\chapter{Boolean Analysis — A Cp Gates}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.RazborovSmolensky.ACpGates
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This file sets up the gate sets $\mathrm{AC}^0$ and $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ over the Boolean
alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}\,2$, and the polynomial machinery used in the Razborov--Smolensky
argument: Razborov's randomized low-degree approximations of unbounded fan-in $\mathrm{OR}$
and $\mathrm{AND}$ over the field $\mathbb{Z}/p$, together with the exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$
polynomial. The main outputs are total-degree bounds of the form $(p-1)\ell$ per gate and
pointwise counting bounds showing that, for each fixed input, at most a $2^{-\ell}$
fraction of the random seeds produce a wrong value.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[The $\mathrm{AC}^0$ gate set]
\lean{ACP.AC_GateOps}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.FeedForward.GateOp.id}
The set of plain $\mathrm{AC}^0$ gate operations on the alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}\,2$: the
identity gate, the NOT gate $x \mapsto 1 - x_0$, and, for every arity $n$, the unbounded
fan-in AND gate $x \mapsto \prod_{i} x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Counting tuples satisfying a pointwise predicate]
\lean{ACP.tuple_fail_count}
\leanok
For a finite index type $\iota$, a finite type $\beta$ and a decidable predicate $P$ on
$\beta$, the number of functions $f : \iota \to \beta$ with $P(f(i))$ for all $i$ equals
$\abs{\{b : P(b)\}}^{\abs{\iota}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging for the probabilistic method]
\lean{ACP.prob_method_averaging}
\leanok
Let $\mathrm{Bad}$ be a finite set of elements of $\alpha$, let $\mathrm{Fail} : \alpha \to
\beta \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be decidable with $\beta$ finite and nonempty, and let $C$ be a
natural number. If for every $a \in \mathrm{Bad}$ we have
$\abs{\{b : \mathrm{Fail}(a,b)\}} \cdot C \le \abs{\beta}$, then there exists a single
$b \in \beta$ with $\abs{\{a \in \mathrm{Bad} : \mathrm{Fail}(a,b)\}} \cdot C \le
\abs{\mathrm{Bad}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Booleanization of a field element]
\lean{ACP.bitify}
\leanok
The map $\mathbb{Z}/p \to \mathrm{Fin}\,2$ sending $a$ to $1$ if $a = 1$ and to $0$
otherwise. It is intended to be applied only to values lying in $\{0,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Booleanization is a section on $\{0,1\}$]
\lean{ACP.cast_bitify_eq}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.bitify}
If $a \in \{0,1\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p$, then casting $\lean{ACP.bitify}\,(a)$ back into
$\mathbb{Z}/p$ through $\mathbb{N}$ recovers $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fermat indicator of zero]
\lean{ACP.one_sub_pow_card_sub_one}
\leanok
For every $a \in \mathbb{Z}/p$ with $p$ prime,
\[
1 - a^{p-1} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } a = 0,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bit indicator agrees with booleanization]
\lean{ACP.bit_indicator_eq_bitify}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.bitify}
If $a \in \{0,1\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p$, then $1 - (1-a)^{p-1}$ equals the cast of
$\lean{ACP.bitify}\,(a)$ into $\mathbb{Z}/p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Unbounded $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ gate]
\lean{ACP.modGateOp}
\leanok
The gate operation of arity \texttt{width} on Boolean inputs that outputs $1$ when the sum
of its inputs, cast into $\mathbb{Z}/p$, is $0$, and outputs $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[{The $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ gate set}]
\lean{ACP.ACp_GateOps}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.AC_GateOps, ACP.modGateOp}
The $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ gate set: the $\mathrm{AC}^0$ gates (identity, NOT, unbounded AND)
together with the unbounded $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ gate of every arity.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized OR-approximating polynomial]
\lean{ACP.approxOr}
\leanok
Given polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_{\mathrm{width}}$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p$ and a random seed
consisting of $\ell$ subsets $S_1,\dots,S_\ell$ of the input positions, the approximator is
\[
1 - \prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\Bigl(1 - \bigl(\textstyle\sum_{i \in S_k} P_i\bigr)^{p-1}\Bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ polynomial]
\lean{ACP.exactMod}
\leanok
The polynomial $1 - \bigl(\sum_i P_i\bigr)^{p-1}$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p$, which computes the
$\mathrm{MOD}_p$ predicate exactly on Boolean values.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Value-level OR approximator]
\lean{ACP.approxOr_val}
\leanok
The value-level analogue of the randomized OR approximator: for $v : \mathrm{Fin}\,
\mathrm{width} \to \mathbb{Z}/p$ and subsets $S_1,\dots,S_\ell$,
\[
1 - \prod_{k}\Bigl(1 - \bigl(\textstyle\sum_{i \in S_k} v_i\bigr)^{p-1}\Bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Value-level OR detector]
\lean{ACP.OR_val}
\leanok
For $v : \mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width} \to \mathbb{Z}/p$, the quantity
$1 - \prod_{k}\bigl(1 - v_k^{\,p-1}\bigr)$, which detects whether some coordinate of $v$ is
nonzero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for the OR approximator]
\lean{ACP.approxOr_totalDegree}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOr}
The total degree of $\lean{ACP.approxOr}$ applied to $P_1,\dots,P_{\mathrm{width}}$ and a
seed $S$ is at most $(p-1)\,\ell \cdot \sup_i \deg(P_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for the exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ polynomial]
\lean{ACP.exactMod_totalDegree}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.exactMod}
The total degree of $\lean{ACP.exactMod}$ applied to $P_1,\dots,P_{\mathrm{width}}$ is at
most $(p-1)\cdot \sup_i \deg(P_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Half the subsets miss a nonzero vector]
\lean{ACP.subset_sum_zero_bound}
\leanok
For a nonzero vector $v : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathbb{Z}/p$, the number of subsets
$s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\sum_{i \in s} v_i = 0$ is at most half of all $2^n$
subsets; formally, twice that count is at most the total number of subsets.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evaluation commutes with the OR approximator]
\lean{ACP.approxOr_eval_eq}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOr, ACP.approxOr_val}
Evaluating $\lean{ACP.approxOr}\,(P, S)$ at a point $y$ gives the same result as applying
the value-level approximator $\lean{ACP.approxOr_val}$ to the evaluated inputs
$i \mapsto P_i(y)$ with the same seed $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Characterization of approximator failure]
\lean{ACP.approxOr_failure_iff}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.OR_val, ACP.approxOr_val, ACP.one_sub_pow_card_sub_one}
For $v : \mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width} \to \mathbb{Z}/p$ and a seed $S$, the value-level
approximator differs from the OR detector if and only if $v \ne 0$ and every seed subset has
vanishing sum, i.e.\ $\sum_{i \in S_k} v_i = 0$ for all $k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bad-seed count for a nonzero input]
\lean{ACP.count_bad_S}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.OR_val, ACP.approxOr_failure_iff, ACP.approxOr_val}
For a nonzero $v$, the number of seeds $S : \mathrm{Fin}\,\ell \to \mathrm{Finset}
(\mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width})$ on which the value-level approximator disagrees with the OR
detector, multiplied by $2^\ell$, is at most the total number of seeds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Number of random seeds]
\lean{ACP.approxSeed_card}
\leanok
The type of seeds $\mathrm{Fin}\,\ell \to \mathrm{Finset}(\mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width})$,
i.e.\ $\ell$ independent subset choices, has cardinality $2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot \ell}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bad-seed bound for every input]
\lean{ACP.count_bad_S_or}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.OR_val, ACP.approxOr_failure_iff, ACP.approxOr_val, ACP.count_bad_S}
Without any nonvanishing hypothesis on $v$: the number of seeds on which the value-level
approximator disagrees with the OR detector, multiplied by $2^\ell$, is at most the total
number of seeds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[List of OR-approximating polynomials]
\lean{ACP.approxOrPolyList}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOr}
The list of all polynomials $\lean{ACP.approxOr}\,(P,S)$, one entry per random seed $S$. It
is a list rather than a set, so a polynomial arising from several seeds appears with the
corresponding multiplicity.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the OR polynomial list]
\lean{ACP.approxOrPolyList_length}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOrPolyList, ACP.approxSeed_card}
The list $\lean{ACP.approxOrPolyList}$ has length $2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise bad-seed count for OR]
\lean{ACP.approxOr_pointwise_bad_count}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.OR_val, ACP.approxOr, ACP.approxOr_eval_eq, ACP.approxSeed_card, ACP.count_bad_S_or}
Fix an evaluation point $y$. The number of seeds $S$ for which
$\lean{ACP.approxOr}\,(P,S)$ evaluated at $y$ differs from
$1 - \prod_k \bigl(1 - P_k(y)^{p-1}\bigr)$, multiplied by $2^\ell$, is at most
$2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$; that is, at most a $2^{-\ell}$ fraction of seeds fail at $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Good OR approximators exist as a distribution]
\lean{ACP.exists_good_approxOr}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOr, ACP.approxOrPolyList, ACP.approxOrPolyList_length, ACP.approxOr_pointwise_bad_count, ACP.approxOr_totalDegree}
There is a list $Ps$ of polynomials, namely $\lean{ACP.approxOrPolyList}\,(P)$, of length
$2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$, every entry of which has total degree at most
$(p-1)\ell\cdot\sup_i \deg(P_i)$, and such that for every evaluation point $y$ the number of
seeds failing to compute the OR value at $y$, times $2^\ell$, is at most the length of $Ps$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Randomized AND-approximating polynomial]
\lean{ACP.approxAnd}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxOr}
The De Morgan dual of the OR approximator: $1 - \lean{ACP.approxOr}\,(1 - P, S)$, where the
approximator is applied to the negated inputs $i \mapsto 1 - P_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for the AND approximator]
\lean{ACP.approxAnd_totalDegree}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxAnd, ACP.approxOr_totalDegree}
The total degree of $\lean{ACP.approxAnd}\,(P,S)$ is at most
$(p-1)\,\ell\cdot\sup_i \deg(P_i)$, the same bound as for the OR approximator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[List of AND-approximating polynomials]
\lean{ACP.approxAndPolyList}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxAnd}
The list of all polynomials $\lean{ACP.approxAnd}\,(P,S)$, one entry per random seed $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the AND polynomial list]
\lean{ACP.approxAndPolyList_length}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxAndPolyList, ACP.approxSeed_card}
The list $\lean{ACP.approxAndPolyList}$ has length $2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise bad-seed count for AND]
\lean{ACP.approxAnd_pointwise_bad_count}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxAnd, ACP.approxOr, ACP.approxOr_pointwise_bad_count}
Fix an evaluation point $y$. The number of seeds $S$ for which
$\lean{ACP.approxAnd}\,(P,S)$ evaluated at $y$ differs from
$\prod_k \bigl(1 - (1 - P_k(y))^{p-1}\bigr)$, multiplied by $2^\ell$, is at most
$2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Good AND approximators exist as a distribution]
\lean{ACP.exists_good_approxAnd}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.approxAnd, ACP.approxAndPolyList, ACP.approxAndPolyList_length, ACP.approxAnd_pointwise_bad_count, ACP.approxAnd_totalDegree}
There is a list $Ps$ of polynomials, namely $\lean{ACP.approxAndPolyList}\,(P)$, of length
$2^{\mathrm{width}\cdot\ell}$, every entry of which has total degree at most
$(p-1)\ell\cdot\sup_i \deg(P_i)$, and such that for every evaluation point $y$ the number of
seeds failing to compute the AND value at $y$, times $2^\ell$, is at most the length of
$Ps$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[{Case analysis on $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ gates}]
\lean{ACP.ACp_GateOps_cases}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.AC_GateOps, ACP.ACp_GateOps, ACP.FeedForward.GateOp.id, ACP.modGateOp}
Every gate operation in $\lean{ACP.ACp_GateOps}$ is one of the following: the identity gate
on a single input, the NOT gate $x \mapsto 1 - x_0$, an unbounded AND gate
$x \mapsto \prod_i x_i$ of some arity $n$, or a $\lean{ACP.modGateOp}$ of some arity $n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ on Boolean inputs]
\lean{ACP.exactMod_on_bits}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.bitify, ACP.cast_bitify_eq, ACP.modGateOp, ACP.one_sub_pow_card_sub_one}
If all values $\mathrm{inputs}_i$ lie in $\{0,1\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p$, then
$1 - \bigl(\sum_i \mathrm{inputs}_i\bigr)^{p-1}$ equals the cast into $\mathbb{Z}/p$ of the
output of the $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ gate applied to the booleanized inputs
$i \mapsto \lean{ACP.bitify}\,(\mathrm{inputs}_i)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact AND on Boolean inputs]
\lean{ACP.exactAnd_on_bits}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.bitify}
If all values $\mathrm{inputs}_i$ lie in $\{0,1\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p$, then
$\prod_i \bigl(1 - (1 - \mathrm{inputs}_i)^{p-1}\bigr)$ equals the cast into $\mathbb{Z}/p$
of $\prod_i \lean{ACP.bitify}\,(\mathrm{inputs}_i)$, the Boolean AND of the booleanized
inputs.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Approximating polynomial family for a single gate]
\lean{ACP.exists_poly_for_gate}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ACp_GateOps, ACP.ACp_GateOps_cases, ACP.approxAnd, ACP.approxAnd_pointwise_bad_count, ACP.approxAnd_totalDegree, ACP.approxSeed_card, ACP.bitify, ACP.cast_bitify_eq, ACP.exactAnd_on_bits, ACP.exactMod, ACP.exactMod_on_bits, ACP.exactMod_totalDegree, ACP.modGateOp}
Let $\mathrm{op}$ be a gate in $\lean{ACP.ACp_GateOps}$ and let $P_i$ be polynomials over
$\mathbb{Z}/p$ computing its inputs. Then there exist a nonempty finite seed type
$\mathrm{Seed}$ with decidable equality and a family $P : \mathrm{Seed} \to
\mathrm{MvPolynomial}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n, \mathbb{Z}/p)$ such that every $P(s)$ has total degree
at most $(p-1)\ell\cdot\sup_i \deg(P_i)$, and for every Boolean input $x$, writing
$y_j = x_j$ cast into $\mathbb{Z}/p$ and $\mathrm{inputs}_i = P_i(y)$, if all
$\mathrm{inputs}_i$ lie in $\{0,1\}$ then the number of seeds $s$ with
$P(s)(y)$ different from the gate value
$\mathrm{op}.\mathrm{func}(i \mapsto \lean{ACP.bitify}(\mathrm{inputs}_i))$, multiplied by
$2^\ell$, is at most $\abs{\mathrm{Seed}}$.
\end{lemma}
